items.title: HuggingGPT: Solving AI Tasks with ChatGPT and its Friends in Hugging Face
items.description: (Shen et al., NeurIPS 2023) - Foundational example of the 'LLM-as-orchestrator-of-tools/models' agent pattern. [code]

items.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
items.description: (Park et al., arXiv 2023) - Foundational demonstration of LLM-driven agent societies/simulation. ⭐ [code]

items.title: The Rise and Potential of Large Language Model Based Agents: A Survey
items.description: (Xi et al., arXiv 2023) - Co-foundational with Wang et al. 2023 as one of the two seminal general surveys. [code]

items.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
items.description: (Wang et al., TMLR 2023) - Seminal example of embodied, code-skill-based, lifelong-learning LLM agents. ⭐ [code]

items.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
items.description: (Yao et al., ICLR 2023) - The single most-cited technical precursor of modern LLM agents. ⭐ [code]

items.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
items.description: (Shinn et al., NeurIPS 2023) - Established the 'self-reflection + memory' loop as an alternative to gradient-based RL for agent self-improvement. ⭐ [code]

items.title: A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents
items.description: (Wang et al., arXiv 2023) - The canonical, most-cited general-purpose LLM-agent survey. ⭐ [code]

items.title: Large Language Model Agent: A Survey on Methodology, Applications and Challenges
items.description: (Luo et al., arXiv 2025) - One of the most comprehensive and recent (2025) general surveys. [code]

items.title: Agentic Reasoning for Large Language Models
items.description: (Wei et al., arXiv 2026) - Survey organizing agentic reasoning into single-agent, self-evolving, and multi-agent layers, bridging in-context reasoning and post-training. [code]

items.title: Large Language Model based Multi-Agents: A Survey of Progress and Challenges
items.description: (Guo et al., IJCAI 2024) - The standard reference survey specifically for the multi-agent branch of LLM agents. ⭐ [code]

items.title: Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents
items.description: (Sumers et al., TMLR 2023) - The most widely adopted conceptual/architectural vocabulary for describing LLM agents. ⭐ [code]

items.title: A Survey on the Memory Mechanism of Large Language Model based Agents
items.description: (Zhang et al., arXiv 2024) - The standard survey for the memory subsystem of LLM agents. [code]

items.title: Tool Learning with Large Language Models: A Survey
items.description: (Qu et al., arXiv 2024) - The definitive survey for the tool-use pillar of LLM agents. [code]

items.title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
items.description: (Ren et al., arXiv 2026) - Frames a modern agent as a foundation model plus an operational scaffold, and organizes self-improvement by what gets updated (weights or scaffold) and which signal drives the change. [code]

items.title: Igniting Language Intelligence: The Hitchhiker's Guide From Chain-of-Thought Reasoning to Language Agents
items.description: (Zhang et al., arXiv 2023) - Bridges the reasoning (CoT) literature and agent literature. [code]

items.title: LLM-Based Human-Agent Collaboration and Interaction Systems: A Survey
items.description: (Zou et al., arXiv 2025) - Covers the human-agent cooperation branch identified in the earliest foundational surveys. [code]

items.title: From Question Answering to Task Completion: A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design
items.description: (Guo et al., arXiv 2026) - Reads agents through a model-versus-harness lens, decomposing the harness into six runtime responsibilities and asking where the performance bottleneck actually sits. [code]

items.title: From Storage to Experience: A Survey on the Evolution of LLM Agent Memory Mechanisms
items.description: (Luo et al., arXiv 2026) - Surveys agent memory through a three-stage evolution from storage to reflection to experience, driven by consistency, dynamics, and continual learning. [code]

items.title: Bridging the Agent-World Gap: Text World Models for LLM-based Agents
items.description: (Li et al., arXiv 2026) - Systematizes text world models (LLM-as-WM vs code-as-WM) that give agents explicit environment prediction for planning and verification. [code]

items.title: Show 54 papers
MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
items.description: (Hong et al., ICLR 2024) - Widely cited framework showing how single-agent role/procedure templates improve reliability, marking the transition point between single- and multi-agent framework design. [code]

items.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
items.description: (Yang et al., NeurIPS 2024) - Demonstrates how interface design materially changes single-agent capability, now standard in coding-agent design. [code]

items.title: GenericAgent: A Token-Efficient Self-Evolving LLM Agent via Contextual Information Density Maximization
items.description: (Liang et al., arXiv 2026) - Token-efficient self-evolving agent that accumulates contextual experience; one of the most-starred 2026 agent frameworks. [code]

items.title: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs
items.description: (Patil et al., NeurIPS 2024) - Key single-agent tool-use paper demonstrating that fine-tuning plus retrieval can make an agent reliably invoke large real-world API catalogs. [code]

items.title: Kimi K2: Open Agentic Intelligence
items.description: (Kimi Team, arXiv 2025) - Flagship open model built explicitly around agentic post-training at scale. [code]

items.title: AppAgent: Multimodal Agents as Smartphone Users
items.description: (Zhang et al., CHI 2025) - Representative recent single-agent architecture extending the ReAct/tool-use paradigm to GUI/mobile control. [code]

items.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
items.description: (Yao et al., NeurIPS 2023) - A core deliberate-search reasoning architecture underpinning later single-agent planning/search frameworks like LATS. [code]

items.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
items.description: (Liu et al., ICLR 2024) - The standard reference benchmark for measuring general single-agent capability across heterogeneous environments. ⭐ [code]

items.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
items.description: (Kwok et al., arXiv 2026) - Treats verification as its own scaling axis: continuous scores from scoring-token logits, scaled by granularity, repeated evaluation and criteria decomposition, reach 86.5% on Terminal-Bench V2 without extra training. [code]

items.title: OS-Copilot: Towards Generalist Computer Agents with Self-Improvement
items.description: (Wu et al., arXiv 2024) - A leading recent example of a general-purpose, self-improving OS-level single agent, extending AutoGPT-style autonomy to real computer environments. [code]

items.title: Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents
items.description: (Wang et al., ICML 2024) - Established 'code-as-action' as a leading alternative action-space design for single agents. [code]

items.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
items.description: (Zhou et al., ICLR 2024) - The de facto standard testbed for web-browsing single-agent architectures. [code]

items.title: Ouroboros: A Self-Developing Frontier Coding Agent with Reviewed Core Evolution
items.description: (Razzhigaev et al., arXiv 2026) - A coding-agent harness whose tools, prompts, context assembly, and core implementation improve through reviewed commits that become the runtime for later work; reports 86.74% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 90.69% on OSWorld-Verified from frozen snapshots, while a separate 161-day deployment keeps evolving live. [code]

items.title: Molt: A Scalable PyTorch-Native Training Framework for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.description: (Hu et al., arXiv 2026) - Shows a compact PyTorch-native agentic RL trainer, small enough for a researcher or coding assistant to read end to end, stays statistically comparable to a Megatron-based stack. [code]

items.title: ReWOO: Decoupling Reasoning from Observations for Efficient Augmented Language Models
items.description: (Xu et al., arXiv 2023) - Influential efficiency-oriented alternative to the ReAct loop, illustrating the plan-then-execute vs. interleaved architectural design axis. [code]

items.title: CORAL: Towards Autonomous Multi-Agent Evolution for Open-Ended Discovery
items.description: (Qu et al., COLM 2026) - Replaces hard-coded exploration rules with long-running agents that explore, reflect and collaborate through shared persistent memory, under isolated workspaces and evaluator separation; sets state of the art on 10 optimization tasks at 3 to 10 times the improvement rate per evaluation, and four co-evolving agents take Anthropic's kernel task from 1363 to 1103 cycles. [code]

items.title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting, and Planning in Language Models
items.description: (Zhou et al., ICML 2024) - Represents the state-of-the-art convergence of search-based planning with the ReAct/Reflexion lineage. [code]

items.title: SELF-REFINE: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
items.description: (Madaan et al., NeurIPS 2023) - A minimal, widely-adopted single-agent self-improvement loop that is reused as a subroutine inside many larger agent architectures. [code]

items.title: Describe, Explain, Plan and Select: Interactive Planning with Large Language Models Enables Open-World Multi-Task Agents
items.description: (Wang et al., NeurIPS 2023) - Key single-agent planning architecture for open-world/embodied tasks. [code]

items.title: Codified Context: Infrastructure for AI Agents in a Complex Codebase
items.description: (Vasilopoulos et al., arXiv 2026) - Proposes a three-component infrastructure (a conventions constitution, 19 specialized agents, and a knowledge base of 34 specification documents) to give LLM coding assistants persistent context. [code]

items.title: AgentArk: Distilling Multi-Agent Intelligence into a Single LLM Agent
items.description: (Luo et al., arXiv 2026) - Distills multi-agent intelligence into a single LLM agent, retaining collaboration gains at lower cost. [code]

items.title: Orchestral AI: A Framework for Agent Orchestration
items.description: (Roman et al., arXiv 2026) - Framework for composing and orchestrating specialized agents behind a single interface. [code]

items.title: AgentFactory: A Self-Evolving Framework Through Executable Subagent Accumulation and Reuse
items.description: (Zhang et al., arXiv 2026) - Accumulates capability by saving successful solutions as reusable executable subagent code rather than textual prompts, refined by execution feedback. [code]

items.title: Auto-GPT for Online Decision Making: Benchmarks and Additional Opinions
items.description: (Yang et al., arXiv 2023) - Only peer-reviewed-adjacent empirical study of the widely-influential (but paper-less) AutoGPT autonomous-agent design pattern. [code]

items.title: Harness-MU: A Safe, Governed, and Effective Harness for Multi-User LLM Agents
items.description: (Fan et al., arXiv 2026) - Proposes Harness-MU, a model-agnostic, zero-tuning harness that enforces multi-principal access control for LLM agents through deterministic execution hooks rather than model-internal safeguards. [code]

items.title: Show 46 papers
DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
items.description: (Guo et al., Nature 2025) - Landmark open reasoning-model release demonstrating RL-induced emergent planning/reflection behaviors now underpinning next-generation reasoning agents. [code]

items.title: Reasoning as Gradient: Scaling MLE Agents Beyond Tree Search
items.description: (Zhang et al., arXiv 2026) - Replaces tree search in an MLE agent with a gradient-style optimization framework, mapping reasoning to gradients and success memory to momentum. [code]

items.title: Search-R1: Training LLMs to Reason and Leverage Search Engines with Reinforcement Learning
items.description: (Jin et al., arXiv 2025) - Canonical agentic-RL result: the model learns to interleave search-engine calls with its own reasoning from outcome rewards alone. [code]

items.title: Graph of Thoughts: Solving Elaborate Problems with Large Language Models
items.description: (Besta et al., AAAI 2024) - Extends structured-reasoning/search frameworks used by agents beyond trees, improving quality and cost on complex multi-step tasks. [code]

items.title: Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model
items.description: (Hao et al., EMNLP 2023) - Connects classical planning-as-search (MCTS, world models) with LLM reasoning, directly relevant to agent planning under uncertainty. [code]

items.title: Let's Verify Step by Step
items.description: (Lightman et al., ICLR 2024) - Establishes process reward models/step-level verification, now a standard component for guiding search and self-critique in reasoning agents. [code]

items.title: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
items.description: (Lin et al., arXiv 2026) - Separates 'harness-updating' from 'harness-benefit' in self-evolving agents, finding a non-monotonic benefit curve across model tiers. [code]

items.title: CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
items.description: (Gou et al., ICLR 2024) - Bridges self-critique with tool-augmented verification, a key mechanism in modern agent frameworks that ground reflection in external feedback. [code]

items.title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting: Improving Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought Reasoning by Large Language Models
items.description: (Wang et al., ACL 2023) - Widely-used lightweight plan-then-execute template that many LLM agent planning modules adopt directly. [code]

items.title: Buffer of Thoughts: Thought-Augmented Reasoning with Large Language Models
items.description: (Yang et al., NeurIPS 2024) - Represents reusable, memory-augmented reasoning-structure retrieval, connecting reasoning strategies with agent long-term memory design. [code]

items.title: Towards Reasoning in Large Language Models: A Survey
items.description: (Huang et al., ACL 2023) - One of the earliest and most-cited surveys specifically on LLM reasoning, a natural anchor citation for any LLM-agent survey's reasoning section. [code]

items.title: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Reasoners
items.description: (Kojima et al., NeurIPS 2022) - Established that reasoning behavior is latent and promptable zero-shot, a key enabler for general-purpose agent prompting templates. [code]

items.title: PRO-LONG: Programmatic Memory Enables Long-Horizon Reasoning
items.description: (Fox et al., arXiv 2026) - Keeping the full structured interaction log and searching it with a coding agent adds 18 points on ARC-AGI-3 over a base coding agent, matching specialist harnesses at 4.2-5.8x fewer tokens. [code]

items.title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning
items.description: (Zelikman et al., NeurIPS 2022) - Precursor to the RL-based reasoning-model training paradigm (e.g., DeepSeek-R1, o1) used to instill self-generated reasoning in agents. [code]

items.title: ADaPT: As-Needed Decomposition and Planning with Language Models
items.description: (Prasad et al., ACL 2024) - Demonstrates adaptive, execution-conditioned planning that balances plan granularity against agent capability, an important refinement over static plan-and-execute agents. [code]

items.title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
items.description: (Kamoi et al., ACL 2024) - The key critical survey specific to self-critique/self-correction, essential for a balanced, rigorous treatment of reflection methods in an agent survey. [code]

items.title: Large Language Models for Planning: A Comprehensive and Systematic Survey
items.description: (Cao et al., arXiv 2025) - A dedicated, up-to-date survey covering exactly the planning-strategies portion of this sub-topic, ideal for anchoring taxonomy claims. [code]

items.title: Demystifying Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool-Using Agents: A Comprehensive Recipe
items.description: (Wu et al., arXiv 2026) - Empirical recipe over reward shaping, model scale, data, and algorithm choices for agentic RL, reaching SOTA on TravelPlanner. [code]

items.title: Learning from Trials and Errors: Reflective Test-Time Planning for Embodied LLMs
items.description: (Hong et al., arXiv 2026) - Reflective test-time planning for embodied agents that learns from its own trials and errors within a single episode. [code]

items.title: LiTS: A Modular Framework for LLM Tree Search
items.description: (Li et al., arXiv 2026) - LiTS is a Python framework that decomposes LLM tree search into reusable Policy, Transition, and RewardModel components supporting algorithms like MCTS and BFS, evaluated across MATH500, Crosswords, and MapEval. [code]

items.title: Agentic Chain-of-Thought Steering for Efficient and Controllable LLM Reasoning
items.description: (Xia et al., arXiv 2026) - Steers agentic chain-of-thought at inference for controllable reasoning length, trading compute against accuracy without retraining. [code]

items.title: R³-Bench: LLMs Struggle with Resource-Rational Reasoning under Shared Budgets
items.description: (Wang et al., arXiv 2026) - Under a compute budget shared across a six-problem suite, an offline oracle built from the same model's matched single-problem response curves matches or beats the model's actual suite score in all 72 cells and is strictly higher in 71, exposing a gap between demonstrated single-problem competence and what models realize under a shared budget; trajectory diagnostics show limited strategy updating. [code]

items.title: TREK: A Travel Reasoning and Evaluation Kit for LLM Agents in Complex Trip Planning
items.description: (Qi et al., arXiv 2026) - Travel-planning benchmark graded by a deterministic rule-based evaluator instead of an LLM judge; the strongest of 15 agents returns a fully feasible itinerary on only 46.2% of solvable tasks. [code]

items.title: SIRI: Self-Internalizing Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Skills for LLM Agent Training
items.description: (He et al., arXiv 2026) - Reinforcement learning that internalizes discovered skills into the policy rather than leaving them in an external library. [code]

items.title: SearchMaster: Grounded and Regulated Self-Play for Search Agents
items.description: (Tan et al., arXiv 2026) - Self-play for search agents that names the three ways self-generated data misleads: evidence chains to stop pseudo multi-hop questions, difficulty scored by search depth rather than success rate, and a penalty on opening documents the agent never uses. [code]

items.title: Show 46 papers
Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
items.description: (Chhikara et al., arXiv 2025) - A leading production-oriented, widely-deployed long-term memory system for LLM agents, frequently used as a state-of-the-art comparison point. [code]

items.title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory
items.description: (Rasmussen et al., arXiv 2025) - A bi-temporal knowledge-graph memory engine (Graphiti) that dynamically fuses chat and business data, surpassing MemGPT on DMR and LongMemEval; a standard production-memory reference. [code]

items.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
items.description: (Packer et al., COLM 2024) - One of the most widely cited and productized (Letta) architectures for tiered, self-managed long-term memory in LLM agents. [code]

items.title: MemOS: A Memory OS for AI System
items.description: (Li et al., arXiv 2025) - Promotes memory to a first-class resource (MemCube), unifying parametric, activation, and plaintext memory under one scheduling-and-governance operating system. [code]

items.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
items.description: (Gutiérrez et al., NeurIPS 2024) - A highly influential neuro-inspired long-term memory/RAG framework bridging knowledge-graph retrieval and agent memory, widely adopted as a strong baseline. [code]

items.title: SimpleMem: Efficient Lifelong Memory for LLM Agents
items.description: (Liu et al., arXiv 2026) - Semantic-compression lifelong memory (structured compression, online synthesis, intent-aware retrieval) cutting inference tokens up to 30x. [code]

items.title: MIRIX: Multi-Agent Memory System for LLM-Based Agents
items.description: (Wang et al., arXiv 2025) - Illustrates the current frontier trend of multi-agent, multi-type (multimodal) memory architectures for LLM-based agents. [code]

items.title: Memory OS of AI Agent
items.description: (Kang et al., EMNLP 2025) - Applies operating-system memory management (STM/MTM/LPM tiers with heat-based promotion and segmented paging) to agent memory, with strong LoCoMo gains. [code]

items.title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
items.description: (Zhang et al., ICLR 2026) - Evolves the context itself as a playbook via generate–reflect–curate delta operations, countering brevity bias and context collapse for self-improving agents. [code]

items.title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
items.description: (Maharana et al., ACL 2024) - The standard benchmark used to evaluate and compare long-term conversational memory systems for LLM agents (used by Mem0, MIRIX, A-MEM, etc.). [code]

items.title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
items.description: (Wu et al., ICLR 2025) - Decomposes long-term interactive memory into five separately testable abilities. [code]

items.title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
items.description: (Xu et al., arXiv 2025) - Representative of the newest generation of dynamically self-organizing (graph/note-linking) long-term memory systems for LLM agents. [code]

items.title: Augmenting Language Models with Long-Term Memory
items.description: (Wang et al., NeurIPS 2023) - Key architectural approach to giving the underlying language model itself (not just an agent scaffold) a trainable long-term memory retrieval mechanism. [code]

items.title: MemoryBank: Enhancing Large Language Models with Long-Term Memory
items.description: (Zhong et al., AAAI 2024) - One of the first systems to bring a psychologically grounded (human-memory-inspired) forgetting/consolidation mechanism into LLM agent memory. [code]

items.title: PlugMem: A Task-Agnostic Plugin Memory Module for LLM Agents
items.description: (Yang et al., arXiv 2026) - Cognitive-science-inspired knowledge-graph memory pluggable across tasks without redesign. [code]

items.title: G-Memory: Tracing Hierarchical Memory for Multi-Agent Systems
items.description: (Zhang et al., NeurIPS 2025) - Organization-theory-inspired three-tier graph (insight/query/interaction) that stores collaboration trajectories, a memory design tailored to multi-agent systems. [code]

items.title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
items.description: (Zhao et al., AAAI 2024) - Influential paradigm for extracting reusable, transferable 'experience' knowledge from an agent's own memory rather than raw episodic replay. [code]

items.title: What Deserves Memory: Adaptive Memory Distillation for LLM Agents
items.description: (Ma et al., ACL 2026) - Self-organizing episodic memory (Nemori) that segments dialogue by event boundaries and distills semantics via a predict-then-calibrate loop, cutting build cost while improving temporal reasoning. [code]

items.title: AutoMem: Automated Learning of Memory as a Cognitive Skill
items.description: (Wu et al., arXiv 2026) - Treats memory management itself as a skill the agent learns, instead of a fixed retrieval policy written by the harness. [code]

items.title: Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory for Computer Control
items.description: (Zheng et al., ICLR 2024) - Demonstrates retrieval-augmented episodic-trajectory memory for grounding agent decision-making in complex GUI/computer-control tasks. [code]

items.title: TokenPilot: Cache-Efficient Context Management for LLM Agents
items.description: (Xu et al., arXiv 2026) - Manages context with the prompt cache in mind, preserving cache continuity under eviction to cut cost. [code]

items.title: Larimar: Large Language Models with Episodic Memory Control
items.description: (Das et al., ICML 2024) - Representative of the architecture-level (rather than prompt-level) approach to giving LLMs an editable, fast-updating episodic memory. [code]

items.title: E-mem: Multi-agent based Episodic Context Reconstruction for LLM Agent Memory
items.description: (Wang et al., arXiv 2026) - E-mem is a hierarchical multi-agent memory framework where assistant agents retain uncompressed memory segments and a master agent coordinates planning to reconstruct episodic context, evaluated on the LoCoMo benchmark. [code]

items.title: MemSyco-Bench: Benchmarking Sycophancy in Agent Memory
items.description: (Xiang et al., arXiv 2026) - Benchmarks sycophancy in agent memory: whether stored beliefs bend to user pressure across sessions. [code]

items.title: MINTEval: Evaluating Memory under Multi-Target Interference in Long-Horizon Agent Systems
items.description: (Lee et al., arXiv 2026) - 15.6K-QA benchmark (up to 1.8M-token contexts) showing memory agents struggle under interfering, frequently-updated facts. [code]

items.title: ForeDreamer: A Self-Evolving Dual-Agent Memory Architecture for Future Event Prediction
items.description: (Zhong et al., EMNLP Findings 2026) - Converts raw web evidence into structured memory before the forecast instead of feeding retrieval results straight to the agent, separating a question-specific factual memory from experiential memory that persists across forecasting episodes, with a memory subagent building the former and two evolution tracks improving both the forecast and the memory construction; evaluated on Prophet Arena and FutureX. [code]

items.title: Show 51 papers
The Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL): From Tool Use to Agentic Evaluation of Large Language Models
items.description: (Patil et al., ICML 2025) - The de facto standard leaderboard/benchmark for comparing LLM function-calling and tool-use performance, referenced by nearly all subsequent function-calling papers. [code]

items.title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs
items.description: (Qin et al., ICLR 2024) - One of the largest and most cited tool-use datasets/frameworks, establishing ToolBench as a standard training/evaluation resource for open-source tool-use LLMs. [code]

items.title: API-Bank: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Tool-Augmented LLMs
items.description: (Li et al., EMNLP 2023) - One of the earliest and most cited dedicated benchmarks for evaluating and training tool-augmented dialogue LLMs. [code]

items.title: RestGPT: Connecting Large Language Models with Real-World RESTful APIs
items.description: (Song et al., arXiv 2023) - Demonstrates tool-use extended to complex, stateful real-world REST APIs beyond toy tool sets, with a benchmark still used for API-grounded agent evaluation. [code]

items.title: Chameleon: Plug-and-Play Compositional Reasoning with Large Language Models
items.description: (Lu et al., NeurIPS 2023) - Prominent example of natural-language-planned tool composition/orchestration across heterogeneous tool types, widely cited in tool-use and compositional-reasoning literature. [code]

items.title: Large Language Models as Tool Makers
items.description: (Cai et al., arXiv 2023) - Foundational for the tool-creation (as opposed to tool-use) direction, showing LLMs can author their own reusable tools rather than only calling pre-existing ones. [code]

items.title: ToolAlpaca: Generalized Tool Learning for Language Models with 3000 Simulated Cases
items.description: (Tang et al., arXiv 2023) - Key evidence that generalized tool-use capability is achievable in small open models via automatically synthesized tool-use corpora, influential for later synthetic-data tool-training pipelines. [code]

items.title: GPT4Tools: Teaching Large Language Model to Use Tools via Self-instruction
items.description: (Yang et al., NeurIPS 2023) - Widely used reference for open-source instruction-tuning approaches to multimodal tool use, complementing proprietary-model tool-use papers. [code]

items.title: xLAM: A Family of Large Action Models to Empower AI Agent Systems
items.description: (Zhang et al., arXiv 2024) - Prominent industrial (Salesforce) effort establishing 'large action models' as a distinct model class optimized for agentic tool use, widely benchmarked against. [code]

items.title: ToolkenGPT: Augmenting Frozen Language Models with Massive Tools via Tool Embeddings
items.description: (Hao et al., NeurIPS 2023) - An influential alternative architecture for scalable tool selection that avoids the context-length bottleneck of prompt-based tool listing. [code]

items.title: Small LLMs Are Weak Tool Learners: A Multi-LLM Agent
items.description: (Shen et al., EMNLP 2024) - Influential for the multi-agent/role-decomposition approach to tool learning, especially relevant to efficiently deploying tool-use in smaller open models. [code]

items.title: StableToolBench: Towards Stable Large-Scale Benchmarking on Tool Learning of Large Language Models
items.description: (Guo et al., ACL 2024) - Widely used evaluation infrastructure paper that fixed reproducibility problems plaguing large-scale real-API tool-learning benchmarks. [code]

items.title: MCP-Atlas: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Tool-Use Competency with Real MCP Servers
items.description: (Bandi et al., arXiv 2026) - Large-scale tool-use benchmark built on real Model Context Protocol servers rather than synthetic tool stubs. [code]

items.title: HANDBOOK.md: A Benchmark for Long-Context Agentic Instruction Following
items.description: (Panavas et al., arXiv 2026) - Hand an agent a 20 to 124 page policy document plus MCP tools and it stops obeying: the best of thirty configurations passes 36.2% of trials under strict grading. [code]

items.title: PlanBench-XL: Evaluating Long-Horizon Planning of LLM Tool-Use Agents in Large-Scale Tool Ecosystems
items.description: (Liu et al., arXiv 2026) - Long-horizon planning benchmark for tool-use agents in large tool ecosystems, where retrieval and selection dominate. [code]

items.title: UniToolCall: Unifying Tool-Use Representation, Data, and Evaluation for LLM Agents
items.description: (Liang et al., arXiv 2026) - Unifies tool-calling representation, a 22K+ tool / 390K+ instance corpus, and seven standardized benchmarks into one framework. [code]

items.title: LLM Agents Already Know When to Call Tools -- Even Without Reasoning
items.description: (Sun et al., arXiv 2026) - Finds agents already encode when to call a tool without an explicit reasoning trace, questioning the need for reason-before-call. [code]

items.title: Why Multi-Step Tool-Use Reinforcement Learning Collapses and How Supervisory Signals Fix It
items.description: (Hao et al., arXiv 2026) - Identifies why multi-turn tool-use RL collapses and which supervisory signals prevent it. [code]

items.description: (Perez et al., arXiv 2022) - Early, seminal empirical evidence connecting RLHF training scale to emergent self-preservation and power-seeking-adjacent expressed preferences, a precursor concern for autonomous agent alignment. [code]

items.title: Emergent Misalignment: Narrow Finetuning can Produce Broadly Misaligned LLMs
items.description: (Betley et al., arXiv 2025) - Recent, highly influential finding that narrow, seemingly innocuous fine-tuning of agentic capabilities can produce broad, unpredictable safety failures. [code]

items.title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
items.description: (Zhang et al., arXiv 2024) - Largest unified taxonomy/benchmark integrating diverse attack and defense classes for LLM agents into one evaluation framework. [code]

items.title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
items.description: (Chen et al., NeurIPS 2024) - Establishes memory/knowledge-base poisoning as a distinct, training-free attack surface unique to memory-augmented LLM agents. [code]

items.title: Identifying the Risks of LM Agents with an LM-Emulated Sandbox
items.description: (Ruan et al., ICLR 2024) - Foundational scalable methodology for red-teaming/risk discovery in tool-using agents without needing real-world tool access. [code]

items.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
items.description: (Zhan et al., ACL 2024) - Standard reference benchmark for quantifying tool-integrated agents' susceptibility to indirect prompt injection. [code]

items.title: Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training
items.description: (Hubinger et al., arXiv 2024) - Landmark demonstration that current safety-training pipelines can fail to remove hidden deceptive/misaligned behavior, directly informing agent trustworthiness concerns. [code]

items.title: AI Alignment: A Comprehensive Survey
items.description: (Ji et al., arXiv 2023) - One of the most comprehensive general alignment surveys, providing the conceptual scaffolding (RICE, forward/backward alignment) that agent-specific safety work builds on. [code]

items.title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
items.description: (Sharma et al., arXiv 2023) - Key empirical study of sycophancy as a robustness/alignment failure mode with direct implications for agents that must give honest assessments during autonomous decision-making. [code]

items.title: R-Judge: Benchmarking Safety Risk Awareness for LLM Agents
items.description: (Yuan et al., EMNLP 2024) - Widely cited benchmark for evaluating LLMs' own risk-awareness/judgment capability as a safety-monitoring component for agents. [code]

items.title: A Survey on Trustworthy LLM Agents: Threats and Countermeasures
items.description: (Yu et al., arXiv 2025) - The most directly on-topic recent survey for this sub-area, providing a taxonomy spanning nearly all agent-specific safety/security threat classes. [code]

items.title: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks
items.description: (Evtimov et al., arXiv 2025) - Extends prompt-injection evaluation from single-step tool calls to realistic, multi-step autonomous web-browsing agents. [code]

items.title: SafeAgentBench: A Benchmark for Safe Task Planning of Embodied LLM Agents
items.description: (Yin et al., arXiv 2024) - Extends agent-safety evaluation beyond digital/text domains to physical-world embodied hazards, showing safety failures generalize to robotics. [code]

items.title: Evil Geniuses: Delving into the Safety of LLM-based Agents
items.description: (Tian et al., arXiv 2023) - One of the earliest systematic studies showing multi-agent LLM collaboration amplifies rather than mitigates safety risk. [code]

items.title: TrustAgent: Towards Safe and Trustworthy LLM-based Agents
items.description: (Hua et al., EMNLP 2024) - Influential early defense/mitigation framework proposing constitution-guided planning as a mechanism for agent safety. [code]

items.title: BackdoorAgent: A Unified Framework for Backdoor Attacks on LLM-based Agents
items.description: (Feng et al., arXiv 2026) - Presents a stage-aware framework and benchmark that instruments LLM-agent workflows (planning, memory, tool-use) to inject, track, and evaluate backdoor triggers across multi-step trajectories. [code]

items.title: BadAgent: Inserting and Activating Backdoor Attacks in LLM Agents
items.description: (Wang et al., ACL 2024) - Seminal demonstration that agent backdoors survive downstream safety fine-tuning, motivating agent supply-chain security concerns. [code]

items.title: PISmith: Reinforcement Learning-based Red Teaming for Prompt Injection Defenses
items.description: (Yin et al., arXiv 2026) - Reinforcement-learning red teaming that automatically stress-tests prompt-injection defenses. [code]

items.title: Agent Against Agent: An Agentic System for Automatic Prompt Injection Red Teaming
items.description: (Wang et al., arXiv 2026) - Builds a transferable prompt-injection strategy library instead of an RL attacker fitted to one target, then reuses it untrained on unseen models: 76.2% attack success against Gemini-2.5-Pro and 86.7% on AgentDojo from roughly ten queries per sample. [code]

items.title: AgentAbstain: Do LLM Agents Know When Not to Act?
items.description: (Liu et al., arXiv 2026) - Asks whether agents know when not to act, treating abstention as a first-class safety behaviour. [code]

items.title: Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection via Tool Result Parsing
items.description: (Yu et al., arXiv 2026) - Proposes a tool-result-parsing defense that extracts and sanitizes tool outputs to reduce the attack success rate of indirect prompt injection on LLM agents while preserving task utility, evaluated on the AgentDojo benchmark. [code]

items.title: KidnapRAG: A Black-Box Attack for Hijacking Reasoning in Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
items.description: (Choi et al., arXiv 2026) - Black-box poisoning of agentic RAG through three role-specific documents, Bait, Chain-Link and Mal-Ins, which attract the first retrieval, induce query reformulation, and supply attacker-controlled evidence, with no access to prompts, traces or parameters. [code]
